title: Completed support coordinates and normalized section restriction
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite normed coefficient field $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Use the actual completed coefficient-system adjunction [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], the integral proper/open operations and realization models [def-sf-integral-system-operations,def-sf-integral-system-realization-data], and compactifications [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Define the separately derived completed-ring word, its proper/open system comparison, its reconstruction-unit transpose q, and the explicit inverse coordinate using the proper comparison and the inverse strict open-reduction map [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison]. On the recorded common cohomological/Tor window with compatible etale origins [def-zl-integral-generator-admissibility-inverse,def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], q is invertible with precisely that inverse, and reduction followed by the actual system counit is the system comparison. For the given realization charts [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization], use the completed coefficient presentation [def-pur-completed-coefficient-presentation-transport] and section encoding [lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization] to define scalar realization and its restriction right adjoint. Ordinary restriction is exact, preserves K-injective complexes, and its restriction/direct-image square is the unique natural isomorphism equal to identity on each underlying section. Derive that square with the canonical composition comparisons. Its left-adjoint conjugate defines the pullback/scalar comparison, and its proper and open mates define the corresponding realization factors. The scalar normalization gives the lattice comparison, and the canonical integral bridge gives the support-system presentation [def-sf-integral-system-canonical-bridge]. These are the original coordinate declarations and three original auxiliary obligations; there is no simultaneous comparison-family existence assertion.

source.place: Definition 6.7.6, Lemma 6.7.14, Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15 give the compactification and coefficient context only. Agent-formulated normalization of the specified comparison maps of lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization, whose proof Steps 2–5, 6 and 13 motivate the formulas; not an assertion literally stated by Bhatt–Scholze. The original coordinate prefix and its auxiliary normalization, identity-on-sections restriction square, and K-injective-preservation statements are preserved verbatim.

proof.text: For integralComparison_normalization, use the representative-normalized invertibility of the fixed open reduction mate (the proved fixedOpenReduction_isIso helper of OpenReconstructionEffectivity); this part needs no quasi-compactness assumption. The Domain hypothesis supplies intrinsic completeness of the open output. Convert it to augmented-tower completeness using sfDerivedComplete_iff_legacy and an auxiliary coefficient test datum. Unrestricted normalized reconstruction then makes the actual reduction/total-limit unit invertible at this open output. Form the composite isomorphism T(unit), then the inverse proper/limit comparison, then L(P(openReduction inverse)). The inverse law of the adjunction Hom equivalence shows that integralComparison is exactly this composite. Naturality of the proper comparison identifies the stated integralInverse with its inverse. The two inverse equations are the isomorphism identities. The final reduction-counit equation is the other inverse identity of the adjunction Hom equivalence. All equations hold before evaluation.

Transport the finite-field characteristic along the injective algebra map and derive the prime/distinct-prime instances. The encoding and completed coefficient charts are equivalences. Compose them with coefficient extension/restriction to obtain realize, restrict, scalarAdjunction and ordinaryRestrict. The restriction factors are exact. Their left adjoints are exact (uniformizer localization is flat), so the ordinary restriction composite preserves K-injective complexes. The ordinary direct image also preserves K-injectives by its exact inverse-image left adjoint.

Coefficient maps are precomposition on continuous sections with the fixed residue and scalar normalizations. The ordinary restriction/direct-image actions therefore coincide on sections. Identity section maps are linear and natural and inverse to each other; faithfulness of the underlying sheaf functor proves uniqueness. This is precisely ordinaryRestrictionSquare_existsUnique and its original proof docstring. Derive that chosen square using the canonical right-derived composition comparisons; K-injective preservation supplies the composition hypotheses.

Take the unique comparison of the left adjoints of the derived restriction square to obtain realizationPull. Its geometric counit mate and open-unit mate give properRealization and openRealizationInverse, respectively, and inverseOrZero gives the forward open factor. The recorded scalar-extension normalization and coefficient/encoding unitors give latticeComparison. Paste the canonical bridge open and proper comparisons to define systemPresentation. All definitions and their actual maps are unchanged; only their implementation module changes.

proof_origin.place: Definitions 6.7.6 and 6.8.1, Lemma 6.7.14 and Proposition 6.8.14(2) provide the coefficient context. R6 proves integralComparison_normalization by the fixed open reduction mate, unrestricted normalized reconstruction, naturality of the specified proper comparison, and the two adjunction Hom-equivalence identities. Remaining scalar-coordinate obligations retain their original statements and proof plans.

lean.statement:
theorem integralComparison_normalization (o : Operations l E)
    (m : RealizationModel l E o) {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (c : Compactification f) (K : Integral l E X) (lo hi a b : ℤ)
    (_hK : Domain l E o c K lo hi a b) :
    IsIso (integralComparison l E o m c K) ∧
    integralComparison l E o m c K ≫ integralInverse l E o m c K = 𝟙 _ ∧
    integralInverse l E o m c K ≫ integralComparison l E o m c K = 𝟙 _ ∧
    (calculus l E Y).reduction.map (integralComparison l E o m c K) ≫
        (calculus l E Y).adjunction.counit.app
          ((Operations.push l E o c.g).obj
            ((Operations.shriek l E o c.i).obj ((calculus l E X).reduction.obj K))) =
      systemComparison l E o m c K
